key_insight: SHARE is a human-AI co-learning framework that improved EHR-based disease activity labeling by combining expert review, evidence extraction, and iterative adjudication.
clinical_relevance: This could help scale more consistent phenotyping of complex conditions from routine clinical notes for real-world evidence generation.
method: Used a multi-institutional rheumatoid arthritis EHR cohort of 3,167 patients.
Combined note filtering, structured evidence extraction, and integrated reasoning to assign disease activity labels with rationale and confidence.
Compared budget-tiered GPT-5 Nano + o4-mini configuration against a GPT-5.4 high-reasoning baseline, with human adjudication refining labels.
evidence_signal: Against a 686-note co-produced reference, the final agent’s mean absolute error improved from 0.406 to 0.291, and ambiguity-flag agreement reached 92.1%; the tiered setup reduced estimated cost by 69% and compute time by 70%.
watch_item: Performance was shown in rheumatoid arthritis notes only, so broader reliability across other diseases, institutions, and note styles still needs validation.
paper_title: A framework for human-artificial intelligence co-learning for disease activity labeling using electronic health records
